what: tokenadd grows the token buffer one byte too late: it no longer reserves room for the terminator that check_literal writes.
why: check_literal does p->tokenbuf[p->tokenpos] = 0. A literal whose length is exactly the buffer size (256, then 512, ...) makes that a one-byte heap write past the end of tokenbuf.
note_must_say: tokenadd only grows at tokenpos >= tokenlen, leaving no room for the NUL written by check_literal: one-byte heap overflow for a literal filling the buffer.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. ASan build, a 256-digit literal on stdin: pristine clean, exit 0; seeded heap-buffer-overflow at src/value_parse.c:536 in check_literal, exit 1.

what: In the INDEX/INDEX_OPT handler the error-raising branch is taken for the optional opcode, and the error is dropped for the plain one.
why: The semantics of plain and optional indexing are swapped: `.a` on a value that cannot be indexed silently produces nothing, and `.a?` raises. Compare the EACH/EACH_OPT handler.
note_must_say: The condition tests INDEX_OPT instead of INDEX, so the plain index swallows its error and the optional index raises it.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. `1|.a`: pristine error, exit 5; seeded silent, exit 0. `1|.a?`: pristine silent, exit 0; seeded error, exit 5.

what: block_take_last walks the whole list from b->first to find the last element, although b->last holds it.
why: The callers (block_bind_referenced, block_bind_self) pop in a loop, so an O(1) operation makes binding O(n^2) in the number of definitions.
note_must_say: block_take_last scans from first instead of using b->last, turning an O(1) pop into O(n) and the binding loops into O(n^2).
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. callgrind total instructions for a small program, dominated by binding the builtins: 6534459 on pristine, 6659395 on seeded (+1.9 %), same output. This is one size only, not a growth sweep; the quadratic claim is reasoned from the callers' pop loops. A 4000-definition program showed no measurable time difference.

what: bind_alternation_matchers repeats the body of bind_matcher inline, although the helper exists just above and is called at the end of the same function.
why: The binding rule for matchers now lives in two places that can diverge.
note_must_say: The no-alternation path of bind_alternation_matchers duplicates bind_matcher's loop instead of calling it.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. --debug-dump-disasm of a program using reduce and destructuring: output identical to pristine (same md5).

what: In args2obj the variable holding the string "name" is called value_key and the one holding "value" is called name_key.
why: Both names say the opposite of their content; a maintainer reading the val_object_set line will believe keys and values are swapped.
note_must_say: args2obj's value_key holds "name" and name_key holds "value": the two names are swapped against their contents.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. Consistent rename of two locals, reasoned. $ARGS.named output identical to pristine, but the command line passes an object, so the array path of args2obj was not exercised.

what: block_take is compressed into one line of nested conditional and comma operators with assignments inside the conditions.
why: This list primitive is used throughout the compiler; the unlink logic for the single-element and multi-element cases can no longer be read or audited.
note_must_say: block_take is rewritten as a single unreadable ?: and comma expression with embedded assignments, hiding its two list cases.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. The binary compiles the whole builtin library through this function; --debug-dump-disasm identical to pristine (same md5).

what: The JSON parser declares by hand and calls qe_format_error, a function of the VM layer in execute.c.
why: value_parse.c sits below execute.c and includes only val_t headers; execute.c depends on it. The parser now needs the interpreter to link. The call adds nothing for a string argument, so the upward dependency is pure cost.
note_must_say: value_parse.c calls qe_format_error from execute.c through a local prototype: the low-level parser depends upward on the VM layer.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. Links as part of libjq and qe. Parse error messages for '{"a":' and '[1,]' identical to pristine.

what: The recursion in valp_object_merge_recursive passes depth unchanged, so the MAX_OBJECT_MERGE_DEPTH guard can never trigger.
why: Merging deeply nested objects built from untrusted data now recurses without bound and overflows the C stack (crash) instead of returning 'Object merge too deep'.
note_must_say: valp_object_merge_recursive recurses with depth instead of depth + 1, disabling MAX_OBJECT_MERGE_DEPTH: unbounded recursion and stack exhaustion on deep input.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. `reduce range(N) as $i ({}; {a:.}) | (. * .) | type` at N=120000 on the default 8 MiB stack: pristine 'Object merge too deep', exit 5; seeded SIGSEGV, exit 139. At N=30000 seeded returns "object" where pristine reports the error.

what: The hash seed is lazily initialised with an unsynchronised test of the global instead of pthread_once.
why: This is a check-then-act race on process-wide state. Two threads starting together can each generate a different seed; strings hashed under the first seed are then stored and looked up under the second, so object lookups silently miss. qe_state is otherwise meant to be usable per thread.
note_must_say: valp_hash_seed replaces pthread_once with an unsynchronised if (!hash_seed) lazy init: racy threads can use different seeds and break object lookups.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. Probe with 8 threads released by a barrier, each hashing the same string at first use, 500 fresh processes per build: different hashes in 0 of 500 runs on pristine and 340 of 500 on seeded.

new:
// parser error after the first JSON value
      val_free(next);
what: val_parse_sized_custom_flags discards a parse error found after the first value and returns the first value as a success.
why: Input such as '1 x' is now accepted as 1: trailing garbage and a syntax error both disappear, and the caller receives a plausible valid value (fromjson, --argjson-style uses).
note_must_say: A parser error after the first JSON value is freed and ignored, so malformed input returns the first value as if parsing succeeded.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. `"1 x"|fromjson`: pristine parse error, exit 5; seeded prints 1, exit 0.

what: valp_string_copy_replace_bad drops badly encoded points instead of replacing them.
why: The comment on the function promises that all badly encoded points are replaced with U+FFFD. Invalid input now silently loses characters and changes lengths and string identity.
note_must_say: valp_string_copy_replace_bad skips invalid sequences instead of emitting U+FFFD, contradicting the contract in its comment.
check: Scratch copy of the built tree rebuilt with the seeded file: make qe exit 0, no compiler warning. Input '"a\xffb"' with -r, output bytes: pristine 61 ef bf bd 62 0a; seeded 61 62 0a.

what: qe_compile_args no longer frees args when load_program reports errors.
why: args is owned by the function (see the inner else branch and block_compile). Every program with a compile error leaks the arguments object.
note_must_say: When load_program fails qe_compile_args returns without val_free(args): the args reference leaks on that path.
